prompt: Why didn't Harvard have calculus classes when it first opened?
answer:
Harvard didn’t offer calculus when it opened in 1636 because calculus had not yet been developed as a formal mathematical discipline. Newton and Leibniz developed its foundational methods independently in the mid-to-late 1600s.

Harvard’s early curriculum instead emphasized classical subjects such as Latin and Greek, theology, logic, arithmetic, geometry, and some algebra. Calculus was added much later, after it had been developed and gradually incorporated into university teaching.
